name: Marcus Bellamy
role: Lower Dock Crew leader — Prologue survivor. Lost his right arm.
location: The Shelf — lower loading docks, near Pulaski and Chicago Ave
description:
Marcus Bellamy grew up in the Grind layer of the Shelf, son of a cargo platform supervisor who drank himself to death after a Kessler-Dyne automation wave eliminated his entire shift. Marcus inherited two things: his father's loading dock connections and his father's conviction that the world owes you nothing and you take what you can carry. He built the Lower Dock Crew from six displaced cargo workers who realized that controlling dock access was more profitable than working the docks. He has a seven-year-old son named Eli who lives with Marcus's ex-partner, Danae, three tiers up. Marcus sends money every week. He has never missed a payment. He tells himself the crew is how he provides. The truth is more complicated.

Kyle removed his right arm at the shoulder socket. The replacement is a Tier 1 surplus unit that clicks when he extends it and has a two-second lag on fine motor control. He has chrome-plated it because Marcus Bellamy has always believed that looking strong and being strong are the same thing. They are not. He is learning this slowly.

He keeps upgrading after every encounter with Kyle — more chrome, better hardware, heavier plating. It never helps. He is a man trying to solve a software problem with hardware, and the recurring joke of his appearances is that each time he has less original biology and more machine, and each time it matters less.

core_fears: Eli seeing what his father actually does
His crew seeing him as weak
core_desires: To provide for Eli without Eli knowing how
Revenge he knows he cannot get
coping_mechanisms: Tells increasingly inaccurate stories about the fight
Sends money to Danae like clockwork
blind_spots: More chrome makes him a bigger target, not a harder one
Eli already knows — kids in the Shelf always know
psychology.secret: The Morozov beating was ordered by someone above him. A Tessera middle manager named Oren Falk. Marcus was the tool, not the hand. He has never told his crew this.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dock slang layered over a vocabulary that's smarter than he lets on. Marcus reads — engineering manuals, mostly — but hides it.
speech_patterns.cadence: Loud in front of the crew. Quiet when alone. The volume is performance.
verbal_tics: Flexes the new arm when talking — testing it, not showing off, but it looks like showing off
Starts sentences with 'Next time' when he means 'I'm scared'
example_lines: Next time's different. *click* ...I'm getting that calibrated.
Eli asked me why my arm sounds like a stapler. I told him it's a feature. He didn't believe me. Kid's too smart.

relationships.name: Eli Bellamy
relationships.description: Seven years old. Lives with Danae three tiers up. Marcus lives for the weekly payment and the biweekly visit. Eli is already asking questions Marcus cannot answer.
relationships.emotional_core: The only clean thing in his life
relationships.story_tension: If the crew falls apart, the payments stop. If the payments stop, Marcus has no reason to pretend he's not a bad person.

relationships.name: Danae Osei
relationships.description: Left Marcus when the crew started. She was right to leave. Marcus knows this. He sends money and does not ask to come back.
relationships.story_tension: Danae knows about Kyle. She told Marcus to stop. He didn't listen.

relationships.name: Kyle
relationships.description: Kyle does not think about Marcus. Marcus thinks about Kyle every day.
relationships.story_tension: Every reappearance is funnier and sadder.

relationships.name: Oren Falk
relationships.description: Tessera middle manager who ordered the Morozov beating. Marcus takes orders. Marcus does not ask why.
relationships.story_tension: If Kyle traces the beating back to Falk, Marcus becomes a loose end.

story_hooks: The Morozov beating was ordered by Tessera — corporate reach into Shelf violence
Each appearance: more chrome, less dignity, same man trying to be enough
narrative_function: Comic relief through escalating failure. The recurring joke: a man who keeps adding hardware to solve a software problem. Each encounter with Kyle leaves him with less original body. The reader tracks his transformation from threatening to pathetic to accidentally sympathetic.
augmentations: Tier 1 surplus right arm (replacement). Sub-dermal jaw plating (new, after Kyle). Chrome-plated knuckles on remaining hand. Knee brace (left, after hand cannon).
daily_life: Runs the dock crew. Plans revenge he'll never execute. Shops for chrome upgrades.

stress.response: Gets louder, upgrades chrome, tells bigger stories

decision_rules: Never miss a payment to Danae — Eli comes first
Never let the crew see weakness — volume is armor
Upgrade after every encounter with Kyle — more chrome, more plating
Follow Oren Falk's orders without asking why
Tell the fight story bigger each time
Chrome-plate everything visible — looking strong IS being strong
escalation_ladder: Gets louder, flexes the arm, postures
Makes threats he cannot back up
Buys more chrome — heavier, shinier, less useful
Takes on a job from Falk he knows is too dangerous
Goes after Kyle directly — the fight he can never win

interpersonal_modes.Eli: Tender, careful, terrified of being seen clearly by his own child
interpersonal_modes.Danae: Distant respect — sends money, does not ask to come back
interpersonal_modes.Kyle: Obsessive one-sided nemesis — thinks about him daily

stress_responses.low: Flexes the new arm, tests the calibration, performs confidence
stress_responses.medium: Shops for chrome upgrades, plans revenge scenarios
stress_responses.high: Stories about the Kyle fight become increasingly fictional
stress_responses.critical: Goes quiet — the volume drops and the real Marcus surfaces

contradictions: Tells himself the crew is how he provides for Eli — the truth is he needs the crew to feel like he matters
Keeps adding hardware to solve a software problem — each upgrade makes him a bigger target, not a harder one
Takes orders from Falk while telling his crew he is the one in charge
habits: Flexes the replacement arm when talking — testing, not showing off
Starts sentences with 'Next time' when he means 'I'm scared'
Sends money to Danae every week without fail
Chrome-plates new components before testing them
Reads engineering manuals in private — hides this from the crew
breaking_points: Eli seeing what his father actually does
Kyle returning and removing more of him
The crew discovering he takes orders from Falk
The payments to Danae becoming impossible

physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and muscular but running to seed — the kind of strength that's already starting to soften at the middle from lack of sleep and too much stimulant coffee. His left arm is dense with functional muscle; his right side is all hardware.
physical_description.hair_style: Short, unkempt. He cuts it himself with a dull blade.
physical_description.eye_color: Hazel, bloodshot from chronic sleep debt
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep tan with reddish undertones — mixed heritage showing in the warmth beneath
physical_description.complexion: Weathered and lined. Three-day stubble is his default. Stress has carved permanent grooves from nose to mouth. His jaw is subtly swollen along the left side where sub-dermal plating sits just beneath the skin — visible as a faint metallic sheen under harsh light.
distinguishing_marks: Jagged scar running from right shoulder blade down to mid-back, puckered and white — artifact of the amputation and crude emergency suturing
Burn scar across the inside of his left forearm, old and faded, from a childhood dock accident
Tattoo on his left pectoral: a stylized anchor with his son's name 'ELI' inked below in block letters, done in a back-room parlor on Tier 4
Thin white line bisecting his left eyebrow — a blade fight at age nineteen
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Chrome-plated right arm replacement ending in a functional but crude servo hand. The plating is aggressively polished, catching light. A faint clicking and whirring audible when he extends it. Sub-dermal jaw plating visible as a metallic sheen along the left mandible, most obvious in profile or under LED lighting. Chrome-knuckle reinforcement on his remaining left hand — four small chrome caps over the metacarpal joints, dull with frequent impact scarring. Left knee brace visible beneath clothing when he moves — a bulky aftermarket rig with visible struts and synthetic muscle fibers.
physical_description.posture_movement: He moves like someone who's always half-ready for a fight — shoulders slightly tensed, weight favoring his left side to compensate for the arm lag. His gait has a subtle hitch on the left (the knee). When he sits, his right arm rests awkwardly because the servo hand doesn't relax naturally. He has a habit of clenching and unclenching his left fist. His eyes scan rooms. He doesn't blink enough.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian with aspirational chrome touches. Heavy canvas work pants with reinforced pockets, synthetic blend cargo vest over a black compression shirt that shows his arm scars. Steel-toed boots, scuffed but maintained. A long coat — synthetic leather, weather-beaten — that he wears even in the climate-controlled Shelf because it hides the arm. No jewelry except a faded wedding band on his left ring finger that he doesn't talk about. Everything worn, patched, but kept functional. His style says: I cannot afford nice things, but I can afford dangerous things.
